But the narrative contradicts itself, and the cited examples and some framing are weak, so an investigator would have to redo some work.","problems":["The headline says 'only 2 of 28 charts below billed' (from the tool output), but the rationale says 1 of 8 documented 99215 claims is below billed. Both are defensible, but the summary never reconciles them.","'Charts support billing' is stated flatly, then followed by hedging about a 32% problems-mismatch rate. This is a conclusion the evidence does not fully support, given the 99215 share of 11.6x expected.","'37% of 99215 claims on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions' is a different cut from the headline's '26% even on no-condition visits'. The summary does not explain that this is a per-complexity-bucket share.","The example C0112769 was documented at moderate MDM with no minutes recorded, so it is a good example. C0112698 and C0112728 are cited only by condition count and add no documentation evidence, and they are probably not among the 28 returned charts.","The summary does not flag the deficiencies in the returned records (MISSING_SIGNATURE, ILLEGIBLE, MISSING_RESULTS), yet it reports 0% unsigned. It mentions 'came after an extension' without giving the delay (57 days).","The next steps are generic ('targeted sample of 99215 charts') and do not say what to look for. They also do not suggest requesting the audit trail, which the summary notes was not received.","The 'inconclusive' leaning sits awkwardly beside a risk-adjusted score of 13.07 and z of 6.1, and the summary does not explain why those figures are discounted."]}
